q-129333.name: Question 3
q-129333.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250894/assets/579e17e56674e39e552f1c0856f40e7f878ed94248a7a0e878c1f851c54ecbea.png)

What is the range of the function $f(x),$ shown above?
q-129333.worked_solution:
First, we find the lowest and highest $y$-values in the graph.

- The lowest $y$-value is $-3.$ This occurs at the point $(3,-3).$

- The highest $y$-value is $1.$ This occurs at the point $(-1,1).$

The function covers all the $y$-values between $-3$ and $1,$ including both $-3$ and $1.$

Therefore, the range is $-3\le y\le 1,$ which can also be written as  $-3\le f(x)\le 1.$

a
−3≤f(x)≤0
b
1≤f(x)≤3
c
−3≤f(x)≤−1
d
−1≤f(x)≤3
e
−3≤f(x)≤1

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the lowest and highest y-values in the graph.

  • The lowest y-value is −3. This occurs at the point (3,−3).

  • The highest y-value is 1. This occurs at the point (−1,1).

The function covers all the y-values between −3 and 1, including both −3 and 1.

Therefore, the range is −3≤y≤1, which can also be written as −3≤f(x)≤1.
